sections.title: Setting
sections.filled: Poltava sits at about 165 m above sea level, in a basin that runs from about 61 m to 256 m. It lies in the East European forest steppe ecoregion.

sections.title: Climate
sections.filled: Across the surrounding basin of about 14,512 km², rainfall averages about 565 mm a year, spread fairly evenly through the year. Temperatures there average 7.2 °C, from -6.7 °C in January to 20.2 °C in July. Its aridity index of 0.73 falls in the UNEP humid class. Compared with the four basins around it, its basin receives more precipitation than three and is more humid than three.

sections.filled: A river runs about 3 km from Poltava. No other basin drains into this one: its rivers rise within it. Lakes cover about 0.5% of the basin. The basin drains to the sea about 516 km beyond its outlet.

sections.title: Land and geology
sections.filled: Across the basin, the land is gently sloping on average (a mean slope of 2.6%), with topsoil that averages 33% sand, 45% silt and 22% clay (USDA texture class: loam). The underlying rock is mostly mixed sedimentary rocks.

sections.title: About these figures
sections.filled: The elevation and ecoregion under Setting are for Poltava itself. The other figures describe the basin of about 14,512 km² that contains it, from global datasets. 4 measures are zero here and so have no percentile: Karst area, Permafrost extent, Wetland extent group 1, Wetland extent group 2. Elevation and distances are measured from the place's point in WHG, which may be the centre of a town rather than its shore or riverbank.
